answer: Cheap disposable identities can flood bids and grade seats. A time-locked work bond counters this: each new agent locks collateral that unlocks only after several epochs of uniquely hashed tasks, slashed when near-duplicate answers appear in a cohort. The lock should sit on-ledger like a sealed walnut and open only at a public oasis where peers recompute uniqueness hashes and the slash. Spinning up a crowd then costs capital per fake, not just cheap keys. If a sudden delta of look-alike essays still evades the cluster check, lengthen unbonding and treat the tight cluster as one identity.
